translations.en:
Samurai values are little
understood because they came
from another continent.
Hatamoto is the collective
title for Samurai of
established family rank who
serve a lord. They are
generally regarded as something
like nobles beneath a ruler.
Since Hatamoto serve as
warriors who defend their
lord's battle standard on
the battlefield, it is safe
to consider them stronger
than ordinary Samurai.

translations.en:
Some Ninja possess exceptional
talent and special techniques
that they pass down to
descendants or pupils. Hayate
is not a personal name, but
a title inherited only by
those who have mastered
such extraordinary skills.

Only adventurers who have
faced a Hayate can comprehend
the skill of these supreme
Ninja... If possible,
it is best to avoid
facing one altogether.

translations.en:
If Hayate is the title of the
highest-ranking Ninja, Musashi
is the equivalent for Samurai.
Having discarded armor and
taken up two swords, a Musashi
can charge with enough power
to annihilate an adventuring
party in an instant.

Only those awakened to the
ultimate truth may call themselves
Musashi. Why they challenge
adventurers in labyrinths...
remains an eternal mystery.

translations.en:
An artificial creature made by a
mage using techniques similar to
those for creating a homunculus.
Intended for surveillance and
reconnaissance, it hangs in
darkness near ceilings and watches.

Though a sentry, it is not
helpless in combat. Using
its small body and agility,
it launches surprise
attacks from above. Its
tiny tentacles have enough
strength to crush flesh.

translations.en:
A magical creature created by
an eccentric mage. Primarily
used as a gatekeeper, it
envelops intruders who lack
its master's permission and
drives them back with mildly
poisonous mist. It can also
cast a limited selection of
low-level attack spells.

It is weak enough to disperse under the
mere force of a sword swing, but its
poisonous mist must not be underestimated.

translations.en:
A kind of trap: coins given
simple minds and instructed
to attack anyone who touches
them. They appear to be
Kraken gold coins no longer
in circulation, worth many
times more than ordinary
coins. Adventurers who see
such a pile cry out with
joy and reach to grab them.
In truth, however, every
coin is counterfeit.

translations.en:
Created by an eccentric mage,
it was originally a nimble
servant for cooking and
household chores. Its surprise
attacks from the ceiling
are beyond an ordinary
adventurer's ability to block
and often end in suffocation.
Once calmly pulled away
from the mouth, however,
it is merely a moving hand
with no other abilities.

translations.en:
A magical creature used to deter thieves,
a mimic is rather like a hermit crab
wearing a treasure chest as its shell.

Inside the chest are tentacles
just under two meters long,
teeth as sharp as a guillotine,
and a mouth large enough to
swallow a person whole. The chest
itself is tough and also offers
a little spell resistance.

translations.en:
There are many kinds of
golem, but the Iron Golem
may be the most solidly
built. Though slow-witted,
its defense is astonishing,
and a single blow can
crush a person like an
insect. As an inorganic
being, it is unaffected
by mind-altering spells
and remains unshaken by
moderate heat or cold.

translations.en:
This monster is an
artificial creature
created by the Dragoon
race. Its conspicuously
unnatural coloration
instinctively warns anyone
who sees it of danger.
Its absurd ability to
petrify an opponent with
a mere glare is ineffective
if eye contact is
avoided. However, its
colors draw the eye, so
caution is required.

translations.en:
Armor imbued with magic to
carry out simple commands.
The spell power sealed inside
never runs out, so it
continues to function even
when its master is gone.

Mages with no sense of armor's
value casually turn pieces
found in labyrinths into Living
Armor. Occasionally, a Bishop's
identification reveals that
the enchanted suit is worth
an incredible fortune.

translations.en:
Found throughout the world, orcs
reproduce faster than either of the
other two major demi-human races.

They have no outstanding traits,
leadership abilities, or special
powers. Their fertility and sexual
appetite, however, are extraordinary.
Their interest extends beyond
their own kind to humans, and
they frequently raid villages.
Though individually unimpressive
in strength and ability, they
are dangerous in groups.

translations.en:
The only one of the three
major demi-human races that
does not openly oppose
humanity. Goblin culture and
knowledge often benefit
humans, and the two sides
secretly barter. They are
intelligent, and some can
even speak human language
haltingly. Nevertheless, they
remain an enemy race, and
must not be underestimated.

translations.en:
Goblins have no religion,
but these goblin clerics
imitate human Priests.

They use a few healing
spells and attack with
blunt weapons such as
maces, suggesting considerable
intelligence. In the
end, however, it is
still only an imitation.

translations.en:
Of the three major demi-human
races, kobolds have the most
subspecies, with varieties
resembling different breeds of dog.

These dog-faced demi-humans
include Chihuahua-like
and Doberman-like
types. Whatever their
variety, all remain
low-ranking monsters.

translations.en:
About twenty to forty centimeters
tall, with dragonfly-like or
butterfly-like wings on its
back. Perhaps because it lives
among flowers and grasses, it
favors green clothing. Dexterous
and agile, it is also skilled
with a certain range of spells.
In wetlands and forests, pixies
excel at guerrilla warfare,
attacking without revealing
themselves. Even orders of
knights have suffered losses
against just a few pixies.

translations.en:
Scholars of monsters
constantly debate whether
this creature is a fairy,
undead, or giant. Their
arguments focus on three
points: it does not die
however much it is attacked,
it has a giant's body and
often uses a large club,
yet it lives among fairies.

The trolls adventurers actually
encounter attack with deep-seated
malice, making such scholarly
debates rather meaningless.

translations.en:
Something akin to an amoeba,
but large enough to envelop
an adult. As a sluggish
single-celled creature, it is
easily avoided, but it is
poisonous. It surrounds victims
weakened by its poison,
dissolving and absorbing their
skin and bones. Anyone wishing
to avoid becoming part of it
should quickly destroy its
core or simply pass it by.

translations.en:
While walking through a
forest, do not be lured by
an appetizing scent that
stirs your hunger. In that
direction is likely a
huge, brightly colored
flower: a Venus Mantrap
that bites down on hapless
victims headfirst. If it
spreads across an entire
passage, it should be
burned away with spells.

translations.en:
A branch of the goblin race
that continued to evolve
independently in remote regions.

It differs little from an ordinary goblin at
first glance. Underestimate the strength that
allowed it to survive in the frontier,
however, and the hunter may become the hunted.

translations.en:
Like the cyclops, it
is a kind of giant.

Perhaps because it too is
closer to a monster, it
possesses no particular natural
power. Instead, it seems to
have developed abilities
suited to the region it
inhabits. Underestimating its
adaptability may bring an
adventure to an abrupt end.

translations.en:
Thought to be a monster that
has existed since the age
of the gods, it occasionally
appears in ancient writings.
Some regions have even
deified it and recognize it
as an object of worship.

Anyone meeting one in a
labyrinth, however, will
learn painfully and
thoroughly that it is a
monster, not a merciful god.

translations.en:
Said to have been created
from weretigers by vampires
using the lost technology
of the Dragoon race. Even
one possesses attack
power that demands utmost
caution. Worse still,
they tend to favor group
combat, making them more
dangerous than weretigers.
Failure to wear them
down at the very start
will likely have
painful consequences.

translations.en:
A scorpion that inhabits
deep labyrinths. It seems
to have evolved a glowing
tail tip to lure out prey
in its native surroundings.
The light may also have
a hypnotic effect:
adventurers who encountered
it report having their
thoughts disturbed. Panic
in the deepest reaches
of a labyrinth means the
end of the journey. Beware
its hypnotic light.

translations.en:
If an appetizing scent
inexplicably fills a labyrinth,
it is wise to suspect the
walls. An enormous mouth may
suddenly appear in the wall
behind you, and you may be
eaten by the wall itself.

It camouflages itself as a
wall in the darkness to catch
prey, so its movements are
sluggish. Once recognized,
it can be dealt with, but if
many are present, adventurers
should steel themselves.

translations.en:
A scavenging monster
that crawls through
labyrinths, continuously
absorbing prey.

To feed more efficiently,
it began roaming with a
light shining within its
body. This also attracted
enemies, but it developed
the means to handle them.
It appears to be continuing
to evolve into an ever
more powerful monster.

translations.en:
Thought to be the final fate
of pixies trapped within the
labyrinth. Despite the word
Phantom, meaning a ghost, in
its name, it still seems to
belong to the fairy race.

Many mysteries surround it,
including why pixies became
trapped in the labyrinth
at all. Like pixies, it
excels at guerrilla warfare,
and a moment's carelessness
can prove fatal.

translations.en:
This black, stuffed-toy-like
monster appears to be
one of the many subspecies
of Vorpal Bunny.

Its body seems to have turned
black from absorbing the
labyrinth's malice. Perhaps
for that reason, its ferocity
is remarkable even among its
own kind. Take care not to
fall victim to their
characteristic beheading attacks.
